title: Account Manager Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion Guide
description: Convert your account manager salary from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, and award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman.
salarySummary: For an account manager on a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the typical account manager salary in Australia?
faqs.a: Account manager salaries vary by industry and experience. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult ordinary time earnings average $2,083.70 per week (May 2026), which annualises to about $108,352. However, many account managers are covered by awards such as the Clerks Award or Professional Employees Award, which set minimum rates. Use the [pay guides](/blog) to check applicable award rates.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual account manager salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by hours per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $35 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $69,160 gross per year. If you are casual, add 25% loading before multiplying. The [the timesheet](/) calculator does this automatically.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include superannuation and tax for an account manager?
faqs.a: Yes. Superannuation is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident rates with the full tax-free threshold and Medicare levy (2%). The result is an estimate only – it does not account for HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Account Manager Salary

If you are an account manager negotiating a new role or reviewing your pay, converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is a practical first step. Most full-time positions in Australia are based on a 38-hour week, and the standard formula is simple: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. This guide explains the calculation, the role of awards and the National Minimum Wage, and how tax and super affect your take-home pay.

### The 38-Hour Week and the Fortnight

We assume a 38-hour week for full-time employees, as this is the ordinary hours standard under many awards and the National Employment Standards. To find your annual gross salary, multiply your hourly rate by 38 and then by 52. For example, an hourly rate of $30 gives $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. If you are paid fortnightly, simply double your weekly pay: weekly gross × 2. This approach is consistent with the Fair Work Ombudsman’s guidance on annualised wages and salaries.

### Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, account managers are often covered by specific awards, such as the Clerks Award or the Professional Employees Award, which set higher minimum rates, penalties, and allowances. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides that list these rates for each classification. Always check the applicable award before relying on the National Minimum Wage. If you are unsure which award applies, use the [pay guides](/blog) on this site to find the correct rates.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual account manager, you are entitled to a 25% loading of 25% on top of the base rate. The casual loading is 25% on top of the base rate – never include it in the hourly rate you type into the calculator. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to calculate it. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12%, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). For the example above, $59,280 gross, the super contribution would be $7,113.60 per year. This is an estimate and does not include salary sacrifice.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross salary is taxed using the 2026–27 resident rates: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2%, but the reduction thresholds used here are the 2025–26 single thresholds (not confirmed for 2026–26). The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page shows net pay after tax and Medicare. Remember, this calculator does not deduct HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Using the Timesheet and Pay Guides

To get a personalised estimate, use the [the timesheet](/) calculator. You enter your base hourly rate and check the casual loading box if applicable. The result shows annual gross, super on top, and estimated net pay. For award-specific rates, refer to the [reference tables](/data) for your classification. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page also has ABS average weekly earnings for full-time adults.

### Example: Account Manager Salary Calculation

Suppose you are a full-time account manager earning $35 per hour. Annual gross = $35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160. Super on top = $69,160 × 12% = $8,299.20. Estimated tax (2026–27) on $69,160: $18,200 tax-free, then $45,000 – $18,200 = $26,800 at 15% = $4,020, then $69,160 – $45,000 = $24,160 at 30% = $7,248, total tax = $11,268. Medicare levy = $69,160 × 2% = $1,383.20. Net annual pay = $69,160 – $11,268 – $1,383.20 = $56,508.80. Fortnightly net = $56,508.80 / 26 = $2,173.42. This example uses the standard assumptions and does not include penalties or allowances.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
